title: Unwrap weight chains and standardize tokenizer gateway
creator: Aisha K. Patel
description: Background: Our current model ingestion pipeline chains multiple weight adapters and tokenizer initialization steps in-process. This has produced fragile coupling between weight-shard activation, checkpoint format detection, and tokenizer handshake logic. Symptoms: long cold-start tails for model activation, memory spikes during concurrent bootstraps, and fragile retries when a shard format detector misclassifies a checkpoint. Goal: break the monolithic 'weight chain' into explicit phases and introduce a small, well-documented 'tokenizer gateway' contract that decouples tokenizer warmup from weight activation. The ticket will: 1) introduce canonical manifest v2 for weight metadata; 2) add a lightweight activation-proxy that performs checksum and lazy shard materialization; 3) extract tokenizer warmup into a separate gateway with clear retry/backoff semantics; 4) add conformance tests and perf benchmarks to prevent regressions. This is a refactor+cleanup (tech debt) — no external API changes expected, but internal artifacts and on-disk manifests will be incremented with backward-compatible readers.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical manifest v2 is defined and documented in the design doc
Loader uses activation-proxy for lazy shard activation in all supported checkpoint formats
Tokenizer gateway provides a stable init API; at least two downstream callers switched (runtime bootstrap and on-demand tokenizer service)
End-to-end cold-start 95th percentile for model activation reduced by >=35% on our staging benchmark
Unit and integration tests added for manifest parsing, activation proxy error modes, and tokenizer gateway retry paths
No customer-facing contract changes; existing checkpoints continue to load via compat reader

comments: 2025-01-13 — Aisha: Created ticket after incident on 2025-01-09 where concurrent model pulls caused OOMs. Linked incident notes and heap profiles.
2025-01-16 — Liam: Spike complete. Prototype activation-proxy reduced peak RSS by ~28% on a 16-shard model. See bench run: https://bench.internal.redwood/model-load/2025-01-16-A-proto

2025-01-20 — Marta Rivera (Design review): Requested clearer semantics around tokenizer gateway idempotency and explicit failure modes. Suggest explicit 'warming' vs 'hydrate' calls. Assigned follow-up to Priya.

2025-01-22 — Priya: Implemented gateway interface with warm() and hydrate() verbs. warm() is idempotent and has backoff; hydrate() triggers shard activation and returns a handle. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4217

2025-01-24 — Owen: Added compat reader for legacy manifests. Edge case: legacy multi-format checkpoints missing checksum — policy: compute on first activation and persist checksum in local manifest cache. Open question: do we write back to upstream stores? Marked as deferred.

2025-01-27 — SRE: Canary plan drafted. Metrics to watch: model_activation.ms_p95, loader.rss.p95, tokenizer.init.ms_p95, activation.errors.rate. Dashboard: https://dash.internal.redwood/load/ingest-cleanup-canary

2025-01-30 — Code review: PR #4217 requested smaller PRs and clearer separation between activation-proxy and scheduler hooks. Owen suggested splitting test-only harness into a separate change to avoid review noise. Liam agreed and updated branch.

2025-02-01 — QA: Added conformance tests covering failure injection (corrupt shard, transient network, checksum mismatch). Tests currently failing in one edge: tokenizer warm() times out under heavy GC; investigating memory pinning during warm path.
follow_up: Decide policy for writing computed checksums back to upstream object store (owner: product + security)
